content.text:
I fixed it: `response.headers.get('set-cookie')` now returns an array of cookies again instead of one comma-joined string.

**Cause:** the response headers were parsed into an array correctly. They were then flattened during response processing, when `normalize()` is called on the headers (from `lib/core/transformData.js`). That method ran every value through `normalizeValue`, which called `String(value)` on it. For an array, that joins the items with commas.

**Fix:** in `lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js`, `normalizeValue` now converts each item of an array to a string and keeps the array. `set()` already had its own special case for arrays, so I removed that and it now just calls `normalizeValue`.

**Checked:** I built headers containing a two-cookie `set-cookie` array and called `normalize(true)`; `get('set-cookie')` returned `['a=1', 'b=2']`. The existing unit tests in `test/unit/core/AxiosHeaders.js` pass (24 passing). I didn't run a full request against a live server or the rest of the test suite.

`toJSON()` still joins array values into one string. That only affects outgoing request headers, so I left it alone.
